title: Projects
description: What you are working on: repositories, and the environments that belong to them.
needsDatabaseHint: They are decisions rather than observations, so they are persisted. Start PostgreSQL and this page comes back; every Docker-backed page works without it.
emptyHint: A Project groups the repositories of one product and the environments running for it. Create one, then attach repositories the GitHub App was granted.

create.title: New workspace
create.description: A name and a slug. Repositories and environments are attached afterwards.
create.name: Name
create.slugHint: Also what a project's portta.project label must say to be adopted automatically.

repositoriesCard.title: Repositories
repositoriesCard.description: From the GitHub App installation. A repository may belong to more than one workspace.
repositoriesCard.emptyHint: Attach one the GitHub App was granted. With no App configured, a workspace still groups environments.

environments.title: Environments
environments.description: Compose projects on this host that belong to this workspace, and why.
environments.empty: Nothing is running for this workspace
environments.emptyHint: Start an environment, label it portta.project with this slug, or link one by hand.

attachRepo.description: Only repositories the GitHub App installation granted can be attached.
attachRepo.hint: Configure the GitHub App under Settings → GitHub and press Sync. A workspace works without it; it just has no repositories.
attachRepo.noneGranted: No repository has been granted yet
attachRepo.noneGrantedHint: Install the GitHub App on the repositories this workspace owns, then press Sync under Settings → GitHub.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: Projected from GitHub. Every row says how old the answer is.
issues.needsDatabaseHint: They are a projection of GitHub, kept locally so they answer while GitHub is unreachable.
